Current Baseline (PAH position): ~72% session utilisation
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: ³85% (GIRFT top quartile)
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Recovering to 85% utilisation across all surgical theatre sessions. Based on GIRFT: bottom-quartile trusts lose 15Ð25% of theatre time. At PAH, a 13pp improvement across ~X sessions/week yields est. 8Ð12 additional cases/week. Source: GIRFT Further Faster 2026.

Current Baseline (PAH position): First patient on table avg 25 mins late
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: Within 15 mins of scheduled start (GIRFT)
PAH Target (to validate): Within 15 mins
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Each 10-min late start across a list loses ~0.5 cases. GIRFT evidence: improving start times to within 15 mins recovers 1 additional case per list per week in high-volume specialties. Low-cost intervention Ñ operational discipline only.

Current Baseline (PAH position): Case durations based on historical averages Ñ known to be inaccurate
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: Procedure-specific GIRFT time norms by surgeon grade
PAH Target (to validate): Adopt GIRFT norms + 10% buffer
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Inaccurate duration assumptions cause underestimation (overruns) or overestimation (underfill). Adopting GIRFT procedure norms improves list fill accuracy. Expected 5Ð8% improvement in cases delivered vs planned. No direct cost Ñ systems and process change only.

Current Baseline (PAH position): Same-day cancellation rate ~8Ð12% (national average)
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: <3% (GIRFT top decile)
PAH Target (to validate): <5% at PAH
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Each same-day cancellation wastes an average of 1.5Ð2 hrs of theatre time. Reducing from ~10% to <5% across PAH elective lists recovers est. 3Ð5 cases/week. Intervention: 2-week readiness checklist, call-before-book, POA alignment. Minimal cost.

Intervention: HVLC pathways Ñ structured on-site lists
Current Baseline (PAH position): HVLC cases mixed into general lists Ñ no dedicated sessions
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: Dedicated HVLC lists: 20Ð30% more cases/session (GIRFT)
PAH Target (to validate): Dedicated HVLC lists in T&O, ophthalmology, ENT, general surgery
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): GIRFT: top-decile trusts with dedicated HVLC lists achieve 20Ð30% more cases per session vs mixed lists. Cataract >95% day case, lap chole >85%, hysteroscopy >90%. At PAH, dedicated HVLC lists in 4 specialties est. to generate 300Ð500 additional cases/yr. Scheduling and clinical engagement only Ñ no capital.

Intervention: HVLC pathways Ñ off-site / community delivery
Current Baseline (PAH position): No off-site HVLC delivery currently
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: 110+ NHS elective hubs nationally; GIRFT: 15Ð25% capacity release from repatriation
PAH Target (to validate): Off-site delivery for ophthalmology and urology Ñ ICS partnership
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Off-site HVLC delivery (cataract, flexible cystoscopy) could release 1Ð2 PAH theatre sessions/week for complex work. Requires ICS partnership agreement, surgeon passporting, patient transport pathway. 3Ð6 month mobilisation. Source: NHSE Elective Hub Programme 2025.

Current Baseline (PAH position): Session utilisation est. ~75%; decontamination turnaround variable
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: ³85% utilisation; standardised decontamination time per procedure
PAH Target (to validate): 85% utilisation; batched procedure lists
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): List optimisation and procedure batching reduces scope changeover and decontamination delays. GIRFT: 10Ð15% throughput improvement achievable through batching alone. No capital Ñ scheduling and standard operating procedure change.

Current Baseline (PAH position): Day case rates below GIRFT benchmark in key specialties
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: Cataract >95%, lap chole >85%, hernia >85%, hysteroscopy >90% (GIRFT)
PAH Target (to validate): Achieve GIRFT top-decile rates in top 5 procedures by volume
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Increasing day case rates frees inpatient beds and increases list throughput. Each overnight stay converted to day case saves est. £800Ð1,200 in bed costs. Across PAH's top 5 HVLC procedures, est. 200Ð350 additional day cases/yr achievable. Requires anaesthetic and surgical practice review.

Current Baseline (PAH position): Majority of POA face-to-face regardless of complexity
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: Telephone-first for ASA 1Ð2 HVLC patients (GIRFT / NHSE)
PAH Target (to validate): Telephone-first for ³60% of POA appointments
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Telephone POA for low-risk patients reduces face-to-face demand by est. 40Ð60% in eligible cohort. Each face-to-face converted to telephone saves ~45 mins of clinical time and estate. Source: NHSE Elective Recovery Guidance 2025.

Current Baseline (PAH position): Anaesthetic review creating delays of 2Ð4 weeks in complex patients
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: Risk-stratified anaesthetic review aligned to surgical complexity (GIRFT)
PAH Target (to validate): Same-week anaesthetic review for planned HVLC cases
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Anaesthetic bottlenecks delay surgical listing and cause same-day cancellations. Aligning anaesthetic review capacity to theatre pipeline removes est. 2Ð3 weeks from patient journey for complex cases. Requires job plan review and potentially additional anaesthetic PA allocation.

Current Baseline (PAH position): Patients routinely re-assessed due to cancellations Ñ duplication estimated at 15Ð20% of POA workload
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: Clear expiry policy; no repeat POA within 6 months for same procedure (NHSE)
PAH Target (to validate): Reduce POA repeat rate to <5%
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Repeat POA due to list cancellations consumes significant clinical capacity with no patient benefit. Estimated 15Ð20% of PAH POA workload is avoidable repeat. Addressing this releases est. 0.5Ð1.0 WTE of POA capacity. Policy and governance change Ñ minimal cost.

Current Baseline (PAH position): Ad hoc prehabilitation; no systematic optimisation programme
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: Structured prehabilitation for high-risk elective patients (NHSE Getting It Right First Time)
PAH Target (to validate): Structured optimisation for top 20% complexity surgical patients
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Perioperative optimisation reduces surgical complications and length of stay. NHSE evidence: prehabilitation programmes reduce post-op LOS by 1Ð2 days in high-risk patients. Financial benefit via reduced bed days. Requires AHP and nursing input Ñ modest investment.

Current Baseline (PAH position): Lists frequently underfilled at 4-week and 2-week mark; no forward-looking fill mechanism
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: 6-4-2 framework: lists confirmed at 6wks, patients confirmed at 4wks, readiness checked at 2wks (GIRFT)
PAH Target (to validate): 6-4-2 framework live across all elective modalities within 6 weeks
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): The single highest-deliverability intervention in the longlist. 6-4-2 discipline eliminates avoidable list underfill. NHSE: trusts implementing structured booking frameworks report 5Ð8% increase in cases delivered per week. Cross-pathway Ñ lifts theatre, outpatients, diagnostics and endoscopy simultaneously. No capital. Process and governance only.

Current Baseline (PAH position): PTL accuracy uncertain Ñ est. 10Ð20% of patients may no longer require treatment (national average)
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: Regular PTL validation with patient contact; 10Ð20% reduction in validated list size (NHSE)
PAH Target (to validate): Validate full PTL; target 10% reduction in active waiters
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): PTL validation identifies patients who have been treated elsewhere, moved, or no longer require treatment. NHSE: average 10Ð20% of waiting list patients can be removed through structured validation. Reduces apparent waiting list size and releases capacity for active patients. NHS App / Patient Portal can automate outreach.

Intervention: Scheduling alignment across POA / theatre / diagnostics
Current Baseline (PAH position): POA, theatre and diagnostic booking managed in silos Ñ misalignment causes delays and cancellations
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: Integrated pipeline scheduling with coordinated milestones (GIRFT Further Faster)
PAH Target (to validate): Aligned scheduling meetings across all three modalities within 8 weeks
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Silo scheduling between POA, theatres and diagnostics results in patients being listed for surgery before POA or investigations are complete. Integrated pipeline reduces avoidable cancellations by est. 2Ð3 percentage points. Process and meeting structure change Ñ minimal cost.

Current Baseline (PAH position): Session utilisation est. ~78%; template fill variable
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: ³85% session utilisation; templates aligned to Royal College norms (GIRFT)
PAH Target (to validate): 85% utilisation; full template audit completed within 4 weeks
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Template standardisation to GIRFT/Royal College norms alone releases 15Ð30% additional clinic capacity at early adopter sites (GIRFT Further Faster Follow-up Collaborative 2026). At PAH est. 1,500Ð3,000 additional OPA slots/yr. No cost Ñ scheduling and clinical governance change.

Current Baseline (PAH position): DNA rate est. 8Ð12% across outpatient specialties
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: <5% DNA rate (GIRFT top decile)
PAH Target (to validate): <6% DNA rate within 6 months
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Each DNA wastes a clinic slot worth est. £150Ð250 (reference cost). Reducing DNA from 10% to 6% across PAH outpatient activity recovers est. 1,000Ð2,000 slots/yr. Interventions: call-before-book, text reminders, overbooking calibration, DNA policy enforcement. Low cost.

Current Baseline (PAH position): New:FU ratio above GIRFT benchmark in multiple specialties Ñ est. 1:3 to 1:5 in some areas
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: 1:2 or better in most specialties (GIRFT top decile)
PAH Target (to validate): Achieve GIRFT benchmark ratio in top 6 volume specialties
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Excess follow-up appointments consume capacity that could be used for new patients. Validated reduction of 20% in follow-up demand redirects est. 2,000Ð4,000 slots/yr to new patients at PAH. GIRFT: follow-ups = 54% of all OPA nationally. Requires clinical protocol review per specialty.

Current Baseline (PAH position): PIFU not systematically implemented; virtual follow-up used ad hoc
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: PIFU in all appropriate pathways by March 2026; ³5% of OPA by March 2029 (NHSE mandate)
PAH Target (to validate): PIFU live in 6 priority specialties within 12 weeks; virtual follow-up expanded
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): PIFU removes routine follow-ups and replaces with patient-initiated contact, releasing scheduled slots. NHSE estimates 1Ð2 million additional slots nationally from PIFU + DIFU + standardised templates combined. At PAH, PIFU in 6 specialties est. to release 800Ð1,500 slots/yr. Requires NHS App integration.

Current Baseline (PAH position): Majority of patients attend first OPA before investigations ordered
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: At least 10 straight-to-test pathways by March 2026 (NHSE mandate)
PAH Target (to validate): 5 pathways live within 3 months; 10 by March 2026
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Straight-to-test enables patients to arrive at first appointment with investigation results, reducing total appointments per episode by 1. NHSE: 8Ð15% referral diversion rate achievable. At PAH, across 10 pathways est. 600Ð1,200 fewer first OPA needed per year. Requires primary care engagement and eRS pathway setup.

Current Baseline (PAH position): Consultation, diagnostics and results managed across multiple visits
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: Single-visit pathways for eligible presentations (GIRFT one-stop model)
PAH Target (to validate): One-stop clinics in 3 high-volume specialties within 6 months
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): One-stop clinics combine consultation, investigation and results in a single visit, reducing total appointments by 1Ð2 per patient episode. Particularly effective in urology (haematuria), gynae (colposcopy) and breast. Patient experience and pathway efficiency both improve significantly. Requires co-located diagnostic capacity.

Current Baseline (PAH position): A&G uptake low Ñ baseline to be confirmed; NHSE target 4m requests nationally in 2025/26
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: 8Ð15% of referrals diverted via A&G at high-performing trusts (NHSE)
PAH Target (to validate): Achieve 10% referral diversion via A&G within 6 months
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): A&G diverts inappropriate or premature referrals before they enter the waiting list. GPs incentivised at £20/request nationally. At PAH, 10% referral diversion across high-volume specialties reduces new OPA demand by est. 800Ð1,500 patients/yr. Requires A&G promotion to primary care and clear response SLAs.

Current Baseline (PAH position): Referrals accepted, rejected or redirected without consistent clinical triage criteria
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: Clinical triage at point of referral in all high-volume specialties (GIRFT)
PAH Target (to validate): Clinical triage live in 8 high-volume specialties within 8 weeks
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Clinical triage at referral ensures patients are directed to the right pathway (OPA, straight-to-test, A&G, community). Reduces inappropriate first OPA by est. 5Ð10%. Requires consultant time for triage Ñ est. 0.5 SPA per specialty. Investment offset by reduction in wasted first appointments.

Current Baseline (PAH position): CT/MRI utilisation below NHS England 4 CT/hr productivity standard in some sessions
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: 4 CT scans/hr (NHSE productivity standard); ³85% modality utilisation
PAH Target (to validate): ³85% utilisation; 4 CT/hr standard achieved within 3 months
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Imaging downtime between patients and suboptimal scheduling reduces modality throughput. NHSE standard: 4 CT scans/hr. Achieving this standard across PAH's CT capacity releases est. 200Ð400 additional scan slots/yr. Session scheduling optimisation and reporting turnaround improvement required.

Current Baseline (PAH position): GP direct access to imaging limited Ñ majority require OPA first
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: GP direct access to MRI and CT for eligible presentations (NHSE straight-to-test)
PAH Target (to validate): Direct access pathway for 5 eligible presentations within 3 months
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Direct access radiology removes the need for an OPA before investigation in eligible presentations (e.g. MSK, suspected hernia, bowel symptoms). Reduces OPA demand by est. 500Ð800 patients/yr. Requires GP education, radiology protocol and eRS pathway setup. Modest cost.

Intervention: Single version of the truth Ñ PTL
Current Baseline (PAH position): Multiple PTL versions in circulation; no single agreed metric set
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: One agreed PTL, one agreed performance dashboard used across the organisation (NHSE)
PAH Target (to validate): Single PTL live and agreed within 4 weeks; dashboard by 8 weeks
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Without a single PTL, capacity planning is inaccurate and interventions cannot be properly targeted or measured. This is a foundational enabler Ñ not directly a capacity intervention but a prerequisite for all others delivering at pace. Systems, governance and data quality resource required.

Current Baseline (PAH position): No real-time elective recovery dashboard by specialty and modality
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: Weekly or real-time specialty-level dashboard (GIRFT Further Faster)
PAH Target (to validate): Live dashboard within 6 weeks covering theatre, OPA, DNA, 18-wk, 52-wk
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Real-time visibility of performance by specialty enables proactive management rather than reactive recovery. Supports 6-4-2 meetings, theatre productivity reviews and outpatient transformation governance. Requires analyst resource and data quality foundation.

Current Baseline (PAH position): Planned vs delivered session variance not systematically tracked
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: <5% variance between planned and delivered DCC sessions (GIRFT)
PAH Target (to validate): Tracker live within 4 weeks; remediation plans for high-variance consultants
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Unexplained session losses are a direct and recoverable productivity gap. If 10% of planned DCC sessions are not delivered, recovering this across PAH's consultant body represents a material throughput gain Ñ equivalent to several additional lists per week. Job plan review and session compliance tracking required.

Current Baseline (PAH position): Nursing and AHP rosters not consistently aligned to elective list demand
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: Rosters demand-led; agency use <5% of elective nursing workforce (NHSE)
PAH Target (to validate): Agency use <5%; rosters aligned to elective lists within 8 weeks
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Agency and bank nursing in elective settings carries a premium cost of est. 25Ð40% above substantive rates. Reducing agency use from current levels to <5% of elective workforce through roster optimisation and substantive recruitment generates direct financial saving. Requires workforce planning resource.

Current Baseline (PAH position): Coding accuracy and activity capture not fully audited Ñ income at risk unknown
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: <2% HRG coding error rate; full activity capture for all elective procedures (NHS standard)
PAH Target (to validate): Full coding audit within 6 weeks; remediation plan within 10 weeks
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Miscoded or uncaptured activity results in direct income loss. National audit data suggests 3Ð8% of elective activity may be miscoded or unclaimed at trusts without robust coding governance. At PAH, a 5% improvement in coding accuracy on elective activity is estimated to recover £1Ð2m in income. Requires clinical coding audit resource.

Current Baseline (PAH position): BPT compliance not systematically reviewed Ñ income opportunity unknown
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: Full BPT compliance for applicable procedures (NHS England)
PAH Target (to validate): BPT compliance audit within 8 weeks; compliance plan within 12 weeks
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Best Practice Tariffs provide additional income for procedures delivered in the optimal pathway (day case, appropriate setting, within timeframe). Non-compliance means income loss. Audit of top 10 BPT procedures at PAH to identify compliance gaps and remediation. Typically £500kÐ£1.5m opportunity at trusts of PAH's size.

Current Baseline (PAH position): No dedicated operational elective recovery control room function
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: Daily elective recovery oversight with escalation capability (NHSE elective recovery framework)
PAH Target (to validate): Control room function live within 4 weeks
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): A dedicated elective recovery control room provides real-time oversight, escalation and intervention when lists are at risk. Prevents avoidable day-of-list failures and enables proactive capacity management. Requires operational lead, analyst support and screen/dashboard infrastructure.

Intervention: Inpatient flow & length of stay impact on elective activity
Current Baseline (PAH position): Elective lists regularly disrupted by emergency pressure on beds Ñ frequency not systematically tracked
GIRFT / NHSE Best Practice Benchmark: <2% elective cancellation rate due to bed unavailability (NHSE standard)
PAH Target (to validate): Track and report elective cancellations due to bed pressure; target <2%
Assumption Detail (lever narrative): Emergency demand cancelling elective lists is one of the most visible and impactful productivity losses. Each cancelled list typically loses 4Ð8 cases. Addressing through improved discharge processes, same-day emergency care, and protected elective bed pools. Requires system-wide coordination.
